title: Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon?: Arrow of the Orion
summary: An 82-minute J.C.Staff theatrical feature (2019-02-15, Warner Bros. Japan) whose story exists nowhere in the owner's instrument: it is an anime-original quest outside Orario, built on a film-only goddess (Artemis), a film-only monster (Antares) and a film-only artefact (the god-made arrow 'Orion'), and it ends with Bell killing Artemis. Four independent lines say 'original', and the licensor is one of them: the official site's own STORY page carries the line 「原作 大森藤ノ先生書き下ろしの完全オリジナルストーリー」 (a completely original story newly written by the author); ja-WP's anime article states 「内容は、原作者書き下ろし脚本だが、原作小説にはないアニメオリジナルストーリーである」; Comic Natalie's announcement (2018-02-18) and ANN's report of the same GA Bunko stage say 「書き下ろしのオリジナルストーリー」 / 'the film will have an original story written by Ōmori'; and danmachi.fandom's film infobox reads Volume = Anime Original. So the standing is filler under T27 — zero standing in the GA Bunko light novel — and Ōmori Fujino's 原作・脚本 credit is a CREDIT in this note, never an adoption (T26): the author himself frames the film as outside the novel line, asking readers who know vol 6 onward to overlook the inconsistencies because 「小説やテレビとは別媒体」. I also checked the DIRECTION on every printed unit that touches the film: the three Ōmori novellas attached to it — 色褪せぬ旅路 (theatre week 1, 2019-02-15, 66pp), One Love (week 2, 2019-02-22, 60pp) and 望まずのストーリーテラー (Blu-ray booklet, 2019-07-31) — are all published on or after release, and the licensor's own giveaway page calls the first 「劇中の空白の十日間を埋めるサイドストーリー」, a side story filling a gap INSIDE the film; a booklet derived from the film cannot be its source, and no novelization exists at all (the NDL, which holds Japan's legal deposit, has no book under オリオンの矢 — only the theme-song CD and the Blu-ray). AniList's LIGHT_NOVEL source tag and its ADAPTATION edge to node 85162 are the franchise tag, not a chapter claim; they are what routed this work into the same-instrument programme.

position.why: Confirmed — and confirmed on CONTENT, not only on the air date, which is the interesting part: the two agree. The task asked whether the licensor sets the film after S2; it does not. The author states the placement himself in the Comic Natalie feature (2019-02-22, interview p2): 「どちらも時系列的にはアニメの1期と2期の間、原作では5巻と6巻の間のお話です」 (どちら = the film and the Memoria Freese 1st-anniversary scenario). The volume boundary lands exactly on our row 13: S1 adapts LN vols 1-5 (ABEMA TIMES' 時系列 list: 「1期／小説1～5巻」; danmachi.fandom's Anime page: 'covering the first five novels'), and vol 5 IS our eps 11-13 (vol 5 = the middle floors, the party stranded, Hestia + Ryuu + Hermes descending, the Monster Rex Goliath — our ep 11 'Labyrinth Utopia (Under Resort)' through ep 13 'The Story of a Familia'), while vol 6 is the Apollo War Game that opens S2 at our ep 14 'Banquet of the Gods (Party)' / ep 15 'Sun God (Apollo)' (fandom: S2 covers 'volumes 6, 7, and part of volume 8'; ABEMA: 「2期／小説6～8巻一部」). Third and independent, en-WP's film article: 'The film takes place between seasons one and two of the anime series.' ABEMA's chronological list places it S1 → Sword Oratoria → S1 OVA → the film → S2. So 13.5 stands: after our ep 13 (2015-06-27, the S1 finale) and before our ep 14 (2019-07-13).

flags_for_sean: TASK PREMISE REFUTED (a claim, not a fact). The task asked whether 'the film is set after S2's events per the licensor'. No source says that, and the author says the opposite: Comic Natalie's feature interview, page 2 — 「どちらも時系列的にはアニメの1期と2期の間、原作では5巻と6巻の間のお話です」. The air-date slot (13.5, because the film opened 2019-02-15 between the 2015 S1 and the July-2019 S2) and the in-universe placement therefore AGREE — this is one of the rare works where the derived position needs no correction and is independently corroborated. The two facts the ask wanted kept apart are the same fact here; I have kept them separate in the note anyway.

THE AUTHOR'S OWN CAVEAT, in the same paragraph, and it is the best evidence against any future adoption claim: 「内容的にはこの時期にやっていいお話ではないんですよね（笑）。敵が強すぎるし、ベルはまだ未熟すぎる。もし本編で劇場版の話をやるのであれば、11巻以降じゃないとベルは太刀打ちできないと思っています」 and 「原作の6巻以降の流れを知っている方が観ると、ちょっと「あれ？」と思ってしまうかもしれないのですが、そこは、小説やテレビとは別媒体ということで、目をつむっていただければ」. The stated slot is authorial INTENT for a story the author deliberately keeps outside the novel's continuity. Under T26 that settles adoption at null: the man who would have to write it into the source line says it is a different medium.

THE DIRECTION QUESTION, answered on the licensor's own page. Three Ōmori-written printed novellas attach to this film and every one of them is downstream of it: 色褪せぬ旅路 (theatre giveaway week 1, from 2019-02-15, 66pp) — the official 前売り・入場特典 page calls it 「劇中の空白の十日間を埋めるサイドストーリー！」 (a side story filling the blank ten days INSIDE the film); One Love (week 2, from 2019-02-22, 60pp) — 「これは、【約束の物語(ファミリア・ミィス)】に至るまでの前日譚(プレリュード)」; 望まずのストーリーテラー (Blu-ray booklet, 2019-07-31). Plus a hard negative on any novelization: the NDL holds NO book under オリオンの矢 (only the theme-song CD and the Blu-ray 特装版), ja-WP's 45-volume GA Bunko inventory has no such title, and danmachi.fandom records Ōmori tweeting that Arrow of Orion sits THIRD on his list of stories he does not want to make into light novels (twitter.com/fujinoomori/status/1274331900518129664 — the wiki's citation; I could not read the tweet itself, so I lean on the NDL and the book lists).

THE FILM'S AFTERLIFE IS IN GAMES, NOT THE NOVEL LINE — park this in case anyone later proposes adoption. Memoria Freese adapted the film as story content and ADDED an epilogue in which Artemis reincarnates and reunites with Bell; the game's 4th-anniversary Aedes Vesta event was called by Ōmori himself 「オリオンの矢 完結編」; DanMachi Battle Chronicle added the film as Story Quests with a further Ōmori short story as sequel/epilogue (danmachi.fandom, 'Continuations'). None of that is the owner's instrument, and T26 does not read a game event as an adoption act.

ORDERING AT 13.x. The S1 OVA ダンジョンに温泉を求めるのは間違っているだろうか (2016-12-07) also sits after our ep 13, and ABEMA TIMES' 時系列 list orders S1 → Sword Oratoria → that OVA → the film → S2. If the OVA is in the halo at 13.x too, the film should sort AFTER it. (Sword Oratoria in that list is a separately owned run, not this owner's.)

AniList's LIGHT_NOVEL source tag and the ADAPTATION edge to node 85162 are the franchise tag trap the protocol names — they are what routed this work into the same-instrument programme, and they carry no chapter claim. The only tie this film has to a printed unit is a SETTING name-drop, not adapted content: vol 2's 間章 already established Hestia / Artemis / Athena as the 三大処女神 (ja-WP cites vol 2 p.135), and Ōmori confirms 「一応、原作の中でもヘスティア、アルテミス、アテナが「三大処女神」であるという設定だけは出していたので」. A pre-existing name in the novels is not a scene the film adapts; chapters_adapted stays empty.

BY-CATCH, OUTSIDE MY ASK — an owner-grid date. My context prints ep 1 as 2015-04-03, a FRIDAY. ja-WP gives S1 as 2015年4月4日 - 6月27日 on TOKYO MX 土曜 1:05-1:35（金曜深夜）, and no station aired earlier (KBS Kyoto 4/5, TV Aichi / AT-X 4/5, BS11 + Sun TV 4/6). Our eps 9-13 (5/30, 6/6, 6/13, 6/20, 6/27) are all Saturdays on that slot and ep 13 matches ja-WP's end date exactly — so ep 1 looks like a Friday −1 reading the rest of the run does not use. I only saw ep 1 and eps 9-13; worth a day-of-week sweep of S1's thirteen rows before anyone repairs anything. S2 is clean: ja-WP's 2019年7月13日 - 9月28日 equals our ep 14 and ep 25.

Kind / title / date all stand — no repairs. ja-WP's film infobox: 公開 2019年2月15日, 上映時間 82分, 監督 桜美かつし, 原作・脚本 大森藤ノ（GA文庫/SBクリエイティブ刊）, 配給 ワーナー・ブラザース映画 — matching the stored kind 'movie' and the AniList date and runtime in my context.
